name: Chettinad Muttai Masala
subtitle: boiled eggs simmered in a roasted coconut and pepper masala

ingredients.qty: 1 point broken off a whole star

prepNotes: Boil the eggs 9 minutes from cold water, then cool them under running water and peel — a full nine minutes gives a set but not chalky yolk.
Score each peeled egg lightly three times with a knife so the masala gets inside.
Roast and grind the masala before you start the gravy; it needs to cool fully before grinding.

steps.text: Dry-roast the red chillies, coriander powder, pepper, fennel, cumin, poppy seeds, stone flower, cinnamon, cloves and star anise over low heat for 4 minutes.
Add the coconut and roast 3 minutes more until it smells toasty and turns pale brown.
steps.tip: Stop while the coconut is still light. Dark coconut makes the gravy taste burnt rather than deep.

steps.text: Cool completely and grind with 100ml water to a smooth paste.
Heat 2 tbsp of the gingelly oil in a kadhai, add the scored eggs with 1/4 tsp turmeric and a pinch of salt, and fry 3 minutes turning until the skins are blistered and golden.
Lift the eggs out and set aside; add the remaining oil and the curry leaves to the same pan.
Fry the shallots for 6 minutes until golden, then add the ginger and garlic pounded to a paste and fry 2 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and remaining turmeric and cook 5 minutes until pulpy and the oil shows at the edges.
Stir in the ground masala and fry on low for 6 minutes until it darkens and the oil separates.
Add 250ml water and salt, bring to a boil, then simmer 8 minutes until the gravy coats the back of a spoon.
Slip the fried eggs in, spoon gravy over them and simmer 5 minutes on the lowest heat.
steps.tip: Do not boil hard with the eggs in — the whites go rubbery. A bare tremble is enough.

steps.text: Rest 5 minutes, scatter the coriander and serve with rice or chapati.

storage: Keeps 2 days refrigerated. Reheat gently on the stovetop; the eggs firm up on standing, so add a splash of water and warm slowly.
